# Canvas backdrop oracle

`canvas-gradient-blur8.rgba` is 128×64 row-major RGBA, captured with Chromium 156.0.8078.4 Canvas2D on 30 October 2026. It is an independent browser filter oracle, not output generated by the native compositor.

The source pixel at `(x,y)` is `[2*x, 4*y, 255-2*x, x < 13 ? 0 : 255]`, matching the owned `tests/fixtures/gradient.png`. Put the source into a separate canvas with `putImageData`. Fill the destination canvas opaque black, set `filter = "blur(8px)"`, draw the source at `(0,0)` without scaling, then read the full destination with `getImageData`.

`gradient_backdrop_matches_chromium_canvas_bytes` checks every byte. Separate native regressions cover black-base opacity, byte source-over products, edge/corner pixels, even box windows and softness 1, 2, 3, 20 and 60. Export-scale and partial-alpha browser reference coverage remains to be expanded.

`canvas-gradient-low-scaled-{1,2,3,4}.rgba` and `canvas-gradient-low-blur8-{1,2,3,4}.rgba` freeze full software Canvas output after a low-quality bilinear RGBA8 resize, followed (for the latter) by blur8 over black. Generate with `node scripts/generate-characters-backdrop-fixtures.mjs` using pinned Chromium156 SwiftShader/software Canvas flags. This two-stage path reproduces the real application2× export; direct cubic resize was a rejected diagnostic. Native tests check every byte at all four scales. A separate controlled partial-alpha oracle catches premultiplication rounding beyond the gradient's0/255 alpha endpoints.

Blur integer-count and scaled-division arithmetic is independently checked against browser fixtures and described by Skia's [ScaledDividerU32](https://skia.googlesource.com/skia/+/b4fb6dbdc017bff5d95fc58d78f8528870610e0b/src/base/SkVx.h) and [ThreeBoxApproxPass](https://github.com/google/skia/blob/main/src/core/SkBlurEngine.cpp).
